boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten verified IU Bloomington study environments, from quiet reading rooms and subject libraries to reservable collaboration spaces.

cards.title: Build the Group Project Here
cards.subtitle: Herman B Wells Library, West Tower first floor
cards.notes: Bring an IU login for the computer workstations, or claim a collaboration room with a whiteboard for a four-to-six-person work session.
cards.short_summary: A technology-equipped collaboration floor with computers, research support, and group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries identifies the Learning Commons as a collaborative academic environment with student computer workstations and first-come, first-served rooms for four to six people equipped with workstations and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Wells Library West Tower. IU credentials are required for computer workstations; listed collaboration rooms are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Settle In Above Tenth Street
cards.subtitle: Herman B Wells Library, East Tower first floor
cards.notes: Choose this room for silent individual reading, then use its periodicals and print references without leaving your study zone.
cards.short_summary: A quiet corner room pairing street-facing views with journals, newspapers, and reference works.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries says the Reference Reading Room occupies the northeast corner of Scholars' Commons, overlooks Tenth Street and North Jordan Avenue, and provides quiet study and print resources for all library patrons.
cards.access_notes: Open to all library patrons on the first floor of the Wells Library East Tower; the room is designated for quiet study.

cards.title: Take the Long Draft Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Herman B Wells Library, East Tower eighth floor
cards.notes: If you are a graduate student, bring a long-form project and choose among tables, benches, couches, or twelve PC workstations.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only quiet workspace with varied seating, computers, printing, outlets, and ethernet.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries places the Grad Commons on the eighth floor of the Wells Library East Tower and documents quiet study, twelve PC workstations, a printer, varied seating, outlets, and ethernet ports.
cards.access_notes: Open to graduate students in all disciplines. IU-sanctioned graduate groups may request the space for Friday events under the posted policies.

cards.title: Study With Playback Tools Nearby
cards.subtitle: Herman B Wells Library ground floor
cards.notes: Use an open table for ordinary coursework, or reserve a five-person media room when your assignment requires collaborative playback technology.
cards.short_summary: Flexible tables, viewing carrels, and reservable media rooms support both coursework and media research.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries documents open individual and group study tables, twelve media-viewing carrels, and four five-person media rooms with whiteboards and collaborative technology.
cards.access_notes: Open study tables serve individuals or groups. Media rooms are reservable, with media-related projects and viewings receiving priority; rooms cannot host office hours.

cards.title: Switch Between Quiet and Group Work
cards.subtitle: Wendell Wright Education Building, room 1160
cards.notes: Start in a quiet area for reading, then reserve an enclosed room when discussion or collaborative lesson planning becomes necessary.
cards.short_summary: A School of Education library combining quiet areas with enclosed reservable group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries describes the Education Library as offering quiet study areas and reservable enclosed group-study spaces on the first floor of the Wendell Wright Education Building.
cards.access_notes: Located in room 1160 on the first floor of the Wendell Wright Education Building. Services and reservable spaces are provided for School of Education affiliates.

cards.title: Connect Four Laptops at One Table
cards.subtitle: Neal-Marshall Center, room A113
cards.notes: Bring a small team to the collaboration table, connect up to four laptops to its large display, or reserve a separate group room.
cards.short_summary: A cultural-resource library with reservable rooms, nine workstations, scanners, and a connected collaboration table.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries documents nine workstations, a large-screen collaboration table connecting as many as four laptops, and group rooms that are reservable or first-come when unreserved.
cards.access_notes: The library serves all IU students, faculty, and staff. Group rooms may be reserved and are open first-come, first-served when not reserved.

cards.title: Book a Room Between Kelley and O’Neill
cards.subtitle: O’Neill SPEA building, room PV 150
cards.notes: Reserve one of fourteen rooms for a one-to-six-person meeting, or use the workstation area when your project needs printing or scanning.
cards.short_summary: A program-focused library with fourteen small-group rooms and a 44-computer technology center.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries locates the Business/SPEA Library where the O’Neill SPEA building meets Hodge Hall and lists fourteen group rooms for one to six users plus 44 computer workstations.
cards.access_notes: Located in PV 150. Group collaboration rooms accommodate one to six users, require a reservation, and may be used for up to two hours.

cards.title: Find the Quiet Floor in the Music Library
cards.subtitle: Simon Music Library and Recital Center
cards.notes: Head to the designated quiet second floor for solo work, or book one of two group rooms when a score or project needs discussion.
cards.short_summary: A four-floor music library offering a quiet level, bookable rooms, carrels, and specialized collections.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries designates Cook Music Library’s second floor as quiet, lists two bookable group rooms, and permits visitors to use unoccupied carrels subject to relocation for the assigned user.
cards.access_notes: Enter the Simon building and take the elevator to floor 1F. Group rooms are bookable; vacant carrels may be used, but users must move if the assigned occupant arrives.

cards.title: Work Below the Chemistry Building
cards.subtitle: Chemistry Building, room C002
cards.notes: Follow the ground-floor signs from the northwest entrance and choose among the library’s quiet, limited-talking, or group-study areas.
cards.short_summary: A science-focused ground-floor library with distinct zones for silent, conversational, and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries locates the Sciences Library in the Chemistry Building, while its current quiet policy identifies quiet, limited-talking, and group-study areas within the library.
cards.access_notes: Located in room C002 at the northwest corner of the Chemistry Building’s ground floor; follow interior signage after entering from the ramped northwest entrance.

cards.entity_name: Wells Library East Tower Quiet Floors
cards.title: Match Your Reading to the Stacks
cards.subtitle: Herman B Wells Library, East Tower floors 4–10
cards.notes: Pick a quiet upper floor near the research collection you need, then settle into one of the tower’s individual study spaces.
cards.short_summary: Seven quiet stack floors combine individual work areas with subject-arranged research collections.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries designates East Tower floors 4 through 10 as quiet-study space and identifies the upper East Tower as home to research stacks and numerous quiet study areas.
cards.access_notes: Use the Wells Library East Tower elevators for floors 4–10. These floors are designated quiet study areas; group work belongs in designated West Tower zones.
